name: Fast Vulkan engines on Pixel 10 Pro (Parakeet + MOSS latency)

description: Baseline: phone_ms=10069 (PK med 2886: mel 26, enc 2612, dec 248; MOSS short 7183: enc+prefill 3675, dec 3280 @102.5ms/tok). Transcripts captured as gate baseline.

asi.baseline_note: Branch head 94230cf. Enc+prefill split missing from this run due to parse bug (fixed); moss enc+prefill=3675 from raw output
asi.hypothesis: Baseline measurement of branch head (PR #287, commit 94230cf): Parakeet medium 2886ms (enc 2612), MOSS short 7183ms (decode 3280, 102.5ms/tok)

description: PowerVR vendor defaults: tile 32,64,4,4 + gemv rows 8 (tuner mis-ranks on real workloads). phone_ms 10069→9363 (PK 2886→2529, enc 2612→2288; MOSS 7183→6834, decode 99.2ms/tok). Transcripts match.

asi.failed_variants: 1) added 32,64,4,4 to candidates only → tuner still picked 64,32 (synthetic ranks it 77.9 vs 82.1ms). 2) barrier-after-every-kernel + norm-interleave in tune recording → still 64,32 (96.7 vs 102.3). 3) M=256→293 (odd tail waves) → still 64,32. Synthetic isolated recordings cannot see the 2x real-workload difference.
asi.hypothesis: Autotuner mis-ranks tiles on PowerVR: synthetic tune picked 64,64,4,4→64,32; real workload wants 32,64,4,4 (2526 vs 2907 med on PK medium) and gemv rows 8
asi.next: Bigger structural items: encoder GEMM kernel itself (subgroup 128 paths), dispatch count reduction, MOSS decode bandwidth

description: PowerVR: f32 GEMM products by default (f16 unpack/pack overhead > full-rate-f32 savings). phone_ms 9363→9261 (PK enc 2288→2262, MOSS enc+prefill 3452→3403). Env STARLING_FAST_F16 still overrides.

asi.hypothesis: Packed-f16 products are a desktop optimization; PowerVR DXT has full-rate f32 so the unpack/pack overhead dominates — f32 products should win
asi.insight: F16MATH path costs ~3% on PowerVR encoders; f32 also strictly improves numerics (products accumulate in f32), so WER gate unaffected by construction

description: Coopmat investigation: driver advertises VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix but shader compiler SEGFAULTS on any coopmat instruction (minimal probe). Kept machinery dormant (STARLING_FAST_COOPMAT=1 opt-in), capability dump in verbose, host glslc preferred. Metric 9285 = thermal noise vs 9261 best (PK enc actually improved to ~2244).

asi.crash_bisect: coopMatStore→shared: crash; coopMatStore→buffer: crash; load+muladd+store: crash; minimal 16x16x16 f16 probe: crash. Compiler segfaults in spvcompiler::LLVMWriter::emitCooperativeMatrixOp regardless of op/storage/instruction mix
asi.driver_details: PowerVR DXT-48-1536, driver 0x00696bd0, api 1.4.317. Reports coopmat 16x16x16+64x16x16 for A/B=FLOAT16 C=FLOAT32, SINT8→SINT32, UINT8→UINT32, scope=3 (subgroup). Enabling vulkanMemoryModel feature did NOT help
asi.glslc_change_side_effect: host glslc 2026.3 now compiles ALL shaders (was NDK 2022.3) — different SPIR-V codegen for scalar kernels; PK enc slightly better (2243 vs 2262), MOSS within thermal noise
asi.hypothesis: VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix (hw f16 matmul) could lift the ~155 GFLOPS GEMM ceiling several fold
asi.next: Scalar-kernel improvements: BK=64 K-tiles (halve barriers), double-buffered tile loads, norm fusion. Revisit coopmat after a PowerVR driver update (probe: coop_probe.comp)

description: BK64 experiment: 64-deep K tiles in scalar GEMM measured WORSE on PowerVR (PK enc 2254→2677ms, -19%). Barriers not the bottleneck; kernel is issue-limited. Discarded (reverted).

asi.bug_found_and_fixed: first BK64 attempt had OOB shared writes ((BM)*(BK/8) bound instead of (BM/2)*(BK/8) row-pairs) — BK32 path corrupted too, encoder 2856ms; fixed bounds restored 2254ms
asi.hypothesis: BK=64 K-tiles halve in-shader barrier count and double compute per barrier → faster GEMM on PowerVR
asi.insight: Barriers between K-slices are NOT the bottleneck (GFLOPS flat ~155 at all M, BK64 worse). The scalar kernel is ALU/issue-limited: per k, 3 shared loads + 3 unpackHalf2x16 + 16 FMA per thread. Without hw matmul (coopmat broken on driver), big GEMM gains need fewer ALU ops per FMA or fewer bytes (int8 dot).
asi.next: Abandon scalar-GEMM micro-tuning; focus on MOSS decode (100ms/token, 11GB/s: lm_head bytes, dispatch count) and PK decoder/mel (CPU side), then norm fusion (fewer dispatches)

description: GEMV RSPLIT: pad workgroups to a full subgroup with parallel row slots (wg=lanes*RSPLIT). MOSS decode 3203→3060ms (95.6ms/tok), phone_ms 9285→9151. W4 K=1024 GEMV 7→13.6 GB/s isolated. Transcripts match; CPU-reference check added to micro probe.

asi.artifact_warning: initial micro '3.5x' was an artifact: local_size_x_id still pointed at LANES so rs>0 threads never ran — 3/4 of rows unwritten (bandwidth inflated 4x, model output broke). Fixed with dedicated WGS spec constant (id 6). Real isolated gain W4 K=1024: 7.0→13.6 GB/s (1.9x)
asi.hypothesis: PowerVR issues whole 128-lane subgroups; GEMV workgroups with lanes=K/32<128 threads waste issue slots → pad workgroup with RSPLIT parallel row slots
asi.instrument: STARLING_FAST_MICRO=bits,N,K[,reps[,rows]] now also verifies GPU vs CPU reference (rel err 0.00000 for W4/W8) — reusable correctness+bandwidth probe

description: PowerVR tile default 32,64,4,4 → 32,128,4,8 (full subgroup + BN=128 halves weight re-reads). phone_ms 9151→8812 (PK enc 2260→2029, MOSS enc+prefill 3404→3056; MOSS decode drift = thermal). Transcripts match. ALU probe: 500 GFLOPS peak vs 155 achieved → still 3x headroom.

asi.alu_probe: pure-FMA probe: ~500 GFLOPS peak (48-192 WGs); GEMM at 155 = 31% of ALU peak — kernel has headroom, not at the wall
asi.config_pattern: best GEMM configs have wg=128 (one PowerVR subgroup) AND BN>=64 (weight re-read amortization): 16,64,4,4 wg=64 → 3836; 64,32,4,4 wg=128 but BN=32 → 5525; 32,128,4,8 wg=128 BN=128 → 1992-2033 BEST; 48/192/256 variants worse (wave quantization)
asi.hypothesis: Tile 32,128,4,8 (wg=128, BN=128 → half the weight re-reads of 32,64) beats 32,64,4,4

description: GEMM shared-tile double-buffering (prefetch next K slice while computing): PK enc 2029→3118ms, 54% WORSE — doubled shared memory halves occupancy. Reverted.

asi.hypothesis: Shared-tile double-buffering hides load latency behind compute (classic GPU GEMM optimization)
asi.insight: On PowerVR occupancy beats latency hiding: doubling shared 10KB→20KB per WG cut resident workgroups and cost 54%. The 155-vs-500 GFLOPS gap is NOT fixable by prefetch scheduling on this GPU; would need less shared per FMA (bigger thread tiles hit register limits) or hw matmul (coopmat broken)

description: PK decoder two-thread GEMV split (persistent spin worker, row-split) + NEON quantize + decode-stage timing. decode 252→201ms (-20%), joint halved. phone_ms 8812→8615. Transcripts match (row split numerically identical).

asi.hypothesis: PK TDT decoder is single-threaded; splitting large GEMV rows across a persistent spin-sync worker thread halves the joint network time
asi.implementation: cpu::GemvHelper: one worker spinning on a seq counter, row-split (numerically identical), split when macs>1M; NEON/AVX2 quantize (nearest-even, saturating) also landed; per-stage decode timing under STARLING_PARAKEET_TIMING
asi.split_breakdown: joint 106→57-67ms, pred 138→124ms, decode total 252→201ms; argmax +3ms (thread contention)

description: Verification rerun: phone_ms 8874 (warm phone; PK stable at ~2288, MOSS decode thermal drift). Session best stands at 8615 (-14.4% vs baseline).

asi.hypothesis: Verification rerun of kept state (4be985e) after energy measurements warmed the phone
asi.note: MOSS decode 3337 vs 3050 in the kept run = thermal drift; PK stable (2288 vs 2293). No code change since last keep.
